research_question: Who finances, operates and supplies energy to DayOne's Batam data-centre infrastructure; what is known about control or dependency; which links cannot be established?

grain_discipline.A_ndp: DayOne Nongsa Digital Park (NDP) campus, Batam — ~72MW IT load across three data centres; financed by the IDR 6.7 trillion (~US$412.1M) DBS/UOB loan (June 2025)
grain_discipline.B_kabil: DayOne Kabil Industrial Tech Park (KITP) campus, Batam — under development; PPA signed 2026-04-17 with PT PLN Batam (~511 MVA ≈ ~450 MW of grid capacity; supply in phases 2026-2027)
grain_discipline.rule: NDP and Kabil are two different campuses of the same operator; the DBS/UOB loan funds NDP (per source wording) and must not be attributed to Kabil; the PLN Batam PPA is grid capacity with no stated energy mix and must not be presented as renewable supply

sources.name: DayOne release — PPA signing (company primary statement)
sources.license: DayOne website release; quoted for research attribution only

exact_passages.quote: DayOne today announced the signing of a landmark set of agreements with PT PLN Batam, marking a major expansion of its digital infrastructure platform in Indonesia. The agreements include the largest long-term power purchase agreement (PPA) in Indonesia, at approximately 511 MVA, equivalent to around 450 MW of grid capacity, as well as memoranda of understanding covering connectivity and electrical infrastructure services for DayOne Kabil Industrial Tech Park (KITP), its new data center campus located in Kabil Integrated Industrial Estate (KIIE), Batam.
Power supply will be delivered in phases between 2026 and 2027 to support the project.
The development represents DayOne’s second hyperscale data center campus in Batam, following its flagship campus in Nongsa Digital Park (NDP)
The DayOne Kabil campus is being developed as a high-performance, AI-ready platform designed to support advanced computing workloads.
strong government support, including the role of BP Batam in facilitating investment, streamlining regulatory processes, and infrastructure development.

supports.kabil_ppa: yes (2026-04-17; ~511 MVA ≈ ~450 MW of GRID capacity; PLN Batam counterparty; KITP named)
supports.supply_schedule: phases 2026-2027 (future commitment at signing; not operational supply)
supports.energy_mix: NOT STATED anywhere in the release — 'grid capacity' only; no renewable claim may be inferred
supports.ai_workload: NO — 'AI-ready platform' is a design/marketing framing

sources.name: Data Center Dynamics — $412m loan article (secondary, quoting company statements and a LinkedIn image)
sources.license: Data Center Dynamics article; quoted for research attribution only (copyright DCD)

exact_passages.quote: Singapore banks DBS and UOB this week announced they have jointly provided an IDR 6.7 trillion ($412.1m) loan facility to DayOne to finance the development of a new data center campus in Batam, Indonesia.

Proceeds of the loan will be used to develop and operate three data centers located in the Nongsa Digital Park (NDP). The first phase is due live by the end of 2025. The campus will have a combined IT load capacity of around 72MW.
GDS spin-out DayOne acquired land in Batam in November 2021 .

The project, jointly developed by DayOne and the Indonesia Investment Authority (INA), is backed by the largest rupiah-denominated financing agreement ever secured for such a development. INA is Indonesia’s sovereign wealth fund, wholly owned by the Government of Indonesia, and partnered with DayOne for the development in 2023 .

This landmark financing — the largest rupiah-denominated facility ever secured for a data centre development — is a strong endorsement of DayOne’s proven ability to deliver digital infrastructure at speed and scale. (Jamie Khoo, CEO of DayOne)

DayOne is the international unit of Chinese data center operator GDS. The company rebranded its Singapore-based international unit at the beginning of this year and has secured outside investment from the likes of SoftBank Vision Fund, Citadel CEO Kenneth Griffin, Coatue Management, and Baupost Group.

supports.ndp_financing: yes (IDR 6.7T / $412.1M, DBS + UOB, for the three NDP data centres)
supports.ina_partnership: yes as reported (jointly developed with INA; partnered 2023)
supports.gds_relationship: mixed/evolving: 'GDS spin-out', 'international unit of GDS', rebranded Jan 2025, outside investors named — the exact current equity relationship is NOT established by this article
supports.kabil_financing: NO — the loan funds NDP; nothing in the article links it to Kabil
